source_name: EUPR / EPTK (FAIR) application system help centre – Támogatott projekt kereső documentation
why_relevant: Documents the underlying data plumbing: the supported-project search draws on EMIR, EUPR and IIER with daily updates. Essential for judging data freshness, field semantics and how to query the system reliably; also names the EPTK/FAIR ecosystem where beneficiaries file claims.

source_name: Központi tényleges tulajdonosi nyilvántartás (TTNY / UBO register, AFAD Act) – NAV information pages
why_relevant: Hungary's central beneficial-ownership register, operated under the AFAD Act. Not open to the public — access is restricted to authorities, supervisors and obliged service providers — but it defines the legal UBO layer and shows what ownership data exists behind the cégjegyzék. Important to document as a known, deliberately closed source so ownership questions are routed to cégkivonat/Opten instead.

source_name: Magyar Innovációs Nagydíj (Hungarian Innovation Grand Prize) – NKFIH / Magyar Innovációs Szövetség
why_relevant: National-level innovation award whose category winners have included financial technology actors (e.g. Péntech Solutions Kft. won the Startup Innovation Award for digital SME financing; an IT development took the 2024 Grand Prize). Award dossiers describe the deployed solution and its customer, giving verified case-study leads.

source_name: Magyar Államkincstár – EU-funded (DIMOP Plusz / KÖFOP) project disclosures
why_relevant: The Treasury and NAV are core state financial-infrastructure beneficiaries; their mandatory project disclosure pages give code, support amount (e.g. HUF 9bn for the complex legal-relationship register), start date and functional scope — direct evidence of state payment/registry IT demand.

source_name: Magyar Nemzeti Bank – procurement notices in the Értesítő (banknote processing / cash-handling machines)
why_relevant: The central bank tenders banknote-processing machines and their maintenance; the notice found is a concrete worked example of the record type this cell targets (buyer, subject, maintenance service). MNB also publishes the list of tested/approved banknote and coin authentication machines, which doubles as a vendor roster.

source_name: Legacy TED notice permalinks (udl?uri=TED:NOTICE:... HU/HTML)
why_relevant: Older Hungarian notices are still reachable via the legacy udl permalink pattern with an explicit HU language token — important for historical backfill because some archive links surface only in this form. Example found: a Hungary-Budapest information-system strategy services notice.

source_name: Bank general terms & conditions / Általános Üzletszabályzat PDFs (static file stores)
why_relevant: General business rules and card T&Cs name the channels, schemes and processing arrangements a bank actually runs (card scheme partners, digital wallet support, outsourced processors) — a technology inventory hiding in legal text.

source_name: MKIK – Modern Vállalkozások Program 2.0 project page (DIMOP_Plusz-1.2.7-23-2023-00001)
why_relevant: Names the exact project code, consortium and operator behind the accreditation catalogue, giving the governance chain (who decides which vendors qualify) and linking chamber, KIFÜ and ministry actors.

source_name: FinTechZone — 'A Nagy Magyar FinTech Történelem' and market coverage
why_relevant: Curated history/landscape of Hungarian fintech vendors, giving founding dates, pivots and acquisitions for local ISVs — valuable context for judging which local competitors are durable versus fading.

source_name: 4iG Nyrt. company profile PDF (Cégbemutató)
why_relevant: Corporate profile deck typically lists business divisions and named sector references, including financial-sector (FinTech) positioning — a compact map of what 4iG claims to hold.

source_name: ANY Biztonsági Nyomda Nyrt. – card manufacture & personalisation (BÉT-listed issuer disclosures)
why_relevant: The dominant Hungarian security printer and card personalisation bureau: Mastercard/Visa chip card production, eID, and the Gránit Bank metal-card project delivered jointly with Thales DIS. Being BÉT-listed, it publishes regulated financial and business reports that quantify the card-personalisation segment — a rare disclosed view of a normally opaque hub.

source_name: Magyar Bankszövetség (hu.wikipedia) – history, membership and organisational overview
why_relevant: Secondary but useful for glossary/alias building and historical continuity (predecessor names, mergers such as the MKB/Budapest Bank/Takarék consolidation into MBH). Not authoritative on current membership — use only to normalise names and catch defunct/renamed entities encountered in archives.

source_name: CARDNET Zrt. – POS terminal operation & transaction processing hub
why_relevant: One of the few Hungarian-owned processing/terminal-estate operators serving banks and acquirers; a direct competitor/partner in the same niche as Printec-type terminal service providers. Company-registry profile gives ownership, financials and group structure.

source_name: Vendor-side confirmation of HU bank deals (iGCB/Intellect, Thought Machine press & fintech trade press)
why_relevant: Banks often stay vague while the winning vendor publishes the specifics; cross-checking bank press rooms against supplier announcements confirms named core-banking wins (OTP–iGCB Intellect Digital Core; Magyar Bankholding/MBH–Thought Machine Vault).

source_name: Mastercard Global Vendor Certification Program (GVCP) — certified card manufacture / personalisation / provisioning vendors
why_relevant: The scheme's certification regime is itself a supplier directory: only GVCP-certified vendors may manufacture/personalise Mastercard cards for issuers. Determines which personalisation bureaus can serve Hungarian issuers. FAQ is public; the certified-vendor listing itself sits behind Mastercard Connect.

source_name: Magyarország Fintech Stratégiája – a hazai pénzügyi szektor digitalizációja (Digitális Jólét Program)
why_relevant: National fintech strategy document produced with industry-association consultation; sets the policy frame that association working groups and member banks respond to, and typically names participating institutions and consultative bodies. Useful as a pointer to which associations sit at the policy table.

entity_name: OPTEN webshop entity pages for payments/banking vendors
source_name: OPTEN webshop entity pages for payments/banking vendors (worked examples)
why_relevant: Concrete proof that the register/aggregator layer resolves the actual actor set for this sector: Diebold Nixdorf Kft. (Vecsés, ex-Wincor Nixdorf Kft., IT/telecom wholesale, FY2024 net revenue reported ~9.45bn HUF), NCR Magyarország Kft., Diebold Hungary Önkiszolgáló Megoldások Kft. 'v.a.' (in voluntary liquidation — an exit signal), Bisnode Magyarország Kft. / Dun & Bradstreet Hungary Kft. These pages give the cégjegyzékszám needed to pull the authoritative beszámoló.

source_name: EU Publications Office — TED reusers workshops Q&A and eForms retrieval guides
why_relevant: Explains the eForms migration, field-level semantics and retrieval patterns. Without this, award-value and winner fields are easy to misparse across the pre-2024 TED schema and the eForms era — a correctness risk for any HU vendor-share metric.

source_name: Government Transparency Institute (govtransparency.eu) — tools and methodology
why_relevant: Documents how the Hungarian procurement data is scraped, cleaned and entity-matched; the methodology tells us which fields are reliable and which HU-specific quirks (buyer name variants, entity IDs) must be normalised before vendor-share analysis.

entity_name: GVH sectoral inquiry into the card-acceptance market
source_name: GVH sectoral inquiry into the card-acceptance market
why_relevant: Hungarian Competition Authority's deep-dive into the acquiring market names the acquirers, their shares, contract structures and terminal economics — rare, evidence-grade competitor intelligence unavailable from vendors.

source_name: Monri Payments blog — republished The Paypers CEE expert view
why_relevant: Illustrates a recurring pattern worth exploiting: paywalled or hard-to-find Paypers expert views on CEE payments are republished in full on the contributing vendor's own site. Vendor mirrors are therefore a practical free route into gated international analyst commentary covering Hungary's region.

source_name: NFSZ / munka.hu – GINOP Plusz-3.2.2-24 flagship project page (employment IT system replacement, consortium with NISZ Zrt.)
why_relevant: Example of a 'kiemelt' (flagship, non-competitive) grant that names the consortium — ministry, county government offices and NISZ Zrt. — and the objective of replacing a legacy state IT system. Flagship-project pages are where large state IT integrator roles become visible early.

source_name: Szintézis Informatikai Zrt. - self-checkout / retail systems integrator
why_relevant: Hungarian IT integrator that publicly documents NCR-based self-checkout deployments in Hungarian stores (reference: a Príma store in Budaörs). Integrator reference pages reveal the vendor-to-buyer chain that procurement notices often hide behind a reseller name.

source_name: Verified Market Research — Hungary POS Terminal Market report
why_relevant: A second, independent syndicated sizing of the Hungarian POS terminal market (2025-2033 horizon) — valuable mainly as a cross-check on Mordor's CAGR and vendor list rather than as a standalone authority.
